INTRODUCTION

1		This memo gives guidance on the UC (NI Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020
1
. The regulations come into force on 24.07.2020.
1 The Universal Credit (Northern Ireland Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020
THE RECIPROCAL ARRANGEMENTS

2		These are reciprocal arrangements for UC between GB and NI (known as territories) and cover claimants moving from one territory to another. Parallel regulations are in place for NI
1
.
1 The UC (GB Reciprocal Arrangements) regulations (NI) 2020
3		Acts omissions or events having effect in GB or NI for the purposes of the relevant legislation are to have corresponding effect in the other territory and in particular—

1.		
a claim for universal credit made in GB or NI has effect as if made in the other territory; 
2.		
residence, presence or employment in GB or NI will have effect as if it were residence, presence or employment in the other territory; 
3.		
any period time served for any purpose in GB or NI has effect as if it were served for a corresponding purpose in the other territory
1
. 
1 The UC (NI Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020 sch, para 2

1.		
a claim for universal credit made in GB or NI has effect as if made in the other territory;

2.		
residence, presence or employment in GB or NI will have effect as if it were residence, presence or employment in the other territory;

3.		
any period time served for any purpose in GB or NI has effect as if it were served for a corresponding purpose in the other territory
1
.
1 The UC (NI Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020 sch, para 2

4 
A decision made in GB or NI can be revised, superseded or heard on appeal in whichever of the two territories the claimant is
1
.
1 The UC (NI Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020 sch, para 3
Example
A person claims UC whilst in GB but is disallowed. That person moves to NI and appeals that decision the appeal can be heard in Northern Ireland.

5		For a revision, supersession or appeal to take place in the other territory, the person must be "in" that territory. A casual presence is not enough
1
.
6		If the person is not "in" that territory, the revision, supersession or appeal must be decided in the territory where the original decision was made.

7		None of the above shall confer a right to double benefit
1
.
1 The UC (NI Reciprocal Arrangements) Regulations 2020 sch, para 4

Requesting case guidance from DMA Leeds for all benefits.
